thread:
Amanda R: incident-bot just paged continuous-batcher in us-east-1 — multiple containers OOMing and a couple nodes flapped, high p99 latency for inference. :rotating_light:
SRE Bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher-prod (us-east-1) - OOM surge x12 in 5m, 2 nodes marked unreachable, error rate spike. Pager routed to #eng-sre and #eng-oncall.
Amanda R: seeing repeated CUDA OOM logs on batcher pods: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` then kubelet killed container.
Raj P: logs? sample pls.
Amanda R: pasted: ```
[2026-03-15T02:12:43Z] batcher: allocate_tokens 98304 -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T02:12:43Z] batcher: falling back to kill request, oom-kill triggered
[2026-03-15T02:12:44Z] runtime: node health flapping, evicting pods
```
Tanya L: looks like continuous prefetch window kept growing. memory footprint climbing long before OOM. can we force-prefetch=0?
Jade (oncall): I'm on it. first step: isolate noisy tenant routes. shifting traffic off node pool us-east-1-b by cordon+drain for affected nodes.
Amanda R: doing `kubectl cordon` now, starting drain. note: we have customers on Dedicated clusters in that pool — CS pinged.
Marco (CS): confirmed a handful of dedicated customers reported 5-10s tail latencies and 500 responses. I'm drafting status note.
Raj P: while draining, we should prevent new large-batch allocations. patching batcher config on the fly: set MAX_BATCH_SIZE=32, PREFETCH_WINDOW=0, KV_PREFETCH=false in the running configmap and rolling restart targeted pods.
Jade (oncall): copying commands: ```kubectl -n inference set env deploy/continuous-batcher MAX_BATCH_SIZE=32 PREFETCH_WINDOW=0 KV_PREFETCH=false``` then rollout restart. doing a canary restart on 2 pods.
DeployBot: deploy started for continuous-batcher:env-change by Jade (oncall) — rollout 2/12 pods restarted.
Amanda R: also reducing grpc_concurrency and lowering per-request kv cache retention: `KV_CACHE_TTL=30s` to reduce resident mem.
Tanya L: good. also enabling fallback policy to smallest compatible model to reduce kv usage: `ROUTING_FALLBACK=small-model`
Raj P: any signs of deadlock or queue starvation from the accumulator?
Amanda R: yes, queue depth climbed then stalled on a subset; we saw backpressure not propagating so accumulation kept adding to batch size until OOM. suspect bug in backpressure signal path between accumulator and prefetcher.
Jade (oncall): mitigation = manual throttle at ingress LB: set request-rate-limit=20rps for affected routes to stop runaway build-up. Applied.
SRE Bot: Observability: p95 latency down from 9.2s to 2.1s after two canary restarts and throttle. error rate dropping.
Marco (CS): customers notified via private thread; one customer escalated to SEs. Marco updating the public status page with: "Degraded performance for inference in us-east-1. Mitigations in progress."
Raj P: we should capture a memory profiler snapshot from a surviving pod before rolling all. Tanya, can you attach gcore or run `python tracemalloc` quick dump?
Tanya L: attaching script: ```kubectl exec -it pod/batcher-xyz -- bash -c 'python - <<PY
import tracemalloc, json
tracemalloc.start()
# trigger short snapshot
s = tracemalloc.take_snapshot()
print(json.dumps([ (f.filename,f.lineno,stat.size) for stat in s.statistics("lineno")[:20] ]))
PY'```
Amanda R: run it on canary pod now — results show big allocations in prefetcher buffers and kv-cache. sending output to #eng-ml for root cause.
Jade (oncall): handoff note for next oncall: we've drained two nodes, throttled ingress, set MAX_BATCH_SIZE=32, PREFETCH_WINDOW=0, KV_CACHE_TTL=30s. Rollout in progress 6/12 pods. p95 down, error rate trending down. still monitoring for node restarts.
Raj P: create an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml. probable root cause: prefetch window growth combined with accumulator backpressure bug. We need a short-term feature flag to cap prefetch window and a longer-term fix to backpressure propagation.
Amanda R: incident ticket created: INC-2026-0442. tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml, and eng-oncall.
Tanya L: forensics note: gather dlmalloc/allocator stats and nvml memory snapshots. will correlate with scheduling events.
Marco (CS): customers updated. CS escalations logged: 3 high-touch customers, 9 minor. Will continue updates.
Jade (oncall): next steps: finish rollout, watch for any new OOMs for 30m, if stable we can un-throttle and incrementally raise MAX_BATCH_SIZE. If nodes continue to flap, we'll spin up extra capacity in another AZ and shift traffic.
Amanda R: thanks team — transferring handoff to Jade (oncall) for next 2h. leaving notes in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
Jade (oncall): taking handoff. summary for next oncall: root cause suspected prefetch/backpressure bug -> Temporary mitigations applied -> follow-ups: postmortem, backpressure fix, add eviction-safe memory limits to batcher, alert refinement for early-prefetch-growth detection.
SRE Bot: HANDOFF logged: oncall -> Jade (oncall).
Jade (oncall): tagging eng-runtime: @Raj P @Tanya L please sync tomorrow for RCA and targeted test to reproduce batch growth locally. I'll keep this thread open for updates.
Amanda R: closing this live triage thread — will append logs to INC-2026-0442.
